item.title: UniCredit to buy back securities-services unit from Societe Generale, document shows
item.description: Italy's second-biggest bank, UniCredit , has signed an agreement to repurchase its securities-services business from French peer Societe Generale , according to a union document seen by Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy's second-biggest bank, UniCredit (CRDI.MI) , has signed an agreement to repurchase its securities-services business from French peer Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) , according to a union document seen by Reuters on Monday. The unit, which looks after investors' securities and handles related administrative services, has 54 staff in Milan and Turin, according to the document, which did not provide any financial details of the agreement. Societe Generale bought UniCredit's securities services unit in 2006, striking a long-term partnership to handle those services for the Italian bank. The supply contract was last renewed in 2017 until 2026. UniCredit is seeking to bring in-house activities it deems strategic, and the transaction is part of that effort, the document said. Handling the securities itself will reduce the need for an external supplier and improve use of the business' data, UniCredit and Societe Generale did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: India flags high unpaid UN dues, raises concern over 2026 liquidity crunch
item.description: India has voiced concern over the "challenging" liquidity situation of the United Nations this year, as it called out the "unacceptably high levels" of unpaid assessments owed by just one member state ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / India flags high unpaid UN dues, raises concern over 2026 liquidity crunch

India flags high unpaid UN dues, raises concern over 2026 liquidity crunch India has raised concern over the UN's liquidity pressures, noting that unpaid regular budget assessments stood at $1.46 billion in 2026, with more than 90% owed by a single member state

Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India United Nations 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 20 2026 | 10:23 AM IST

Listen to This Article

India has voiced concern over the "challenging" liquidity situation of the United Nations this year, as it called out the "unacceptably high levels" of unpaid assessments owed by just one member state. "We consider that full, timely and unconditional payment of assessed contribution is the Charter obligation of every Member State," Counsellor in the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Surendra Adhana said here Monday. Adhana delivered India's national statement at the 81st Main Session of the Fifth Committee of the UN General Assembly on 'Improving the financial situation of the United Nations'. "We note with concern that the liquidity situation in 2026 remained challenging due to the collection uncertainties and low cash balance," he said.

"While we have noted the marginal drop in the regular budget unpaid assessment to $1.46 billion from the $1.87 billion a year ago, the reality is that the unpaid assessment continued to remain at unacceptably high levels, and over 90 per cent of the regular budget arrears are owed by one member state," he said. Also Read

India urges vigilance on weapons tech transfers to terror-linked actors

UN food agency cuts aid to Palestinians in Gaza, West Bank amid fund crunch

Banks tap RBI's first cash auction in 3 months as market rates spike

India rejects UN expert's report on youth freedom, asks to verify claims

India asks UN human rights office to seek answers from Pakistan on PoK

The US is the single largest financial contributor to the UN, paying 22 per cent of the regular budget and 27per cent of the peacekeeping budget. In September, Washington paid $725 million to the UN regular budget and an additional $102 million for peacekeeping. But the US still owes the UN over $4 billion for its regular budget and peacekeeping arrears.

Adhana noted that the respite resulting from a strong collection in the third quarter needs to be sustained. India welcomed that 141 member states had paid in full their assessment by September 30 this year compared to 136 member states last year. India also voiced concern over the financial situation in UN peacekeeping, describing it as "more worrisome". Adhana noted that unpaid assessments for UN peacekeeping reached $4.1 billion, up from $3.7 billion last year, while collection stagnated at around 1.4 billion. "Two member states alone account for roughly 88 per cent of this amount," he said. US and China are the top two contributors to UN peacekeeping. China paid $641.4 million in September for its regular UN budget contributions.

"We urge all Member States, especially those with requisite means, to take expeditious action to fulfill their financial obligations. This is critical to ensuring a financially healthy and sound United Nations with zero indebtedness. It is an integral part of our common quest for prudent budgetary and financial management of the organisation," he said. India has consistently paid its assessment in full, on time, and often in advance. This year, India was among the 55 Member States that paid their regular budget assessments in full within the 30 day due period. India made a payment of $35.18 million in February this year.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: National Australia Bank to cut 2,500 jobs in cost overhaul as credit growth slows
item.description: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Tuesday it will shed up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in the next year to simplify its operations and cut costs while the nation's credit growth remains under pressure.
item.dc:creator: Scott Murdoch, Rajasik Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB.AX) said on Tuesday it will shed up to 2,500 jobs, or about 6% of its workforce, in the next year to simplify its operations and cut costs while the nation's credit growth remains under pressure. The bank, which is Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender, said up to 1,500 roles would go by the end of 2026. The biggest cuts will target corporate roles rather than customer-facing bankers, it said. It also plans to materially reduce its use of consultants and contractors. "Our ambition and strategy remain unchanged. We will improve productivity, risk outcomes and execution to be a simpler and more efficient bank," Chief Executive Andrew Irvine said in a statement. NAB stock was down nearly 2.5% on Tuesday, and recorded the largest share price decline of Australia's "Big Four" retail banks in the session. The S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) was down 0.9%. NAB said it would begin consultation with the Finance Sector Union, whose national assistant secretary Nicole McPherson said the job cuts would not help simplify the organisation. "To take a wrecking ball to 6% of one of Australia's largest workforces this close to Christmas is disgraceful and shows that NAB's leadership is completely detached from the lived experience of their workers," she said. The overhaul will result in a restructuring charge of about A$300 million ($209 million) before tax in 2027, related to redundancy, redeployment and organisational redesign costs. The charge compares with about A$80 million before tax incurred in each of 2025 and 2026, NAB said. The job cuts follow a period of mounting pressure on Australia's banks as weaker housing activity, rising competition and higher operating costs weigh on earnings. [USN:L1N44D060 TEXT:"In August"], NAB warned that housing credit growth would slow sharply in 2027 following the [USN:L4N42409E TEXT:"federal government's property tax"] reforms, which the bank said had dampened demand from homebuyers and investors. At that time, Irvine said the combined effects of geopolitical uncertainty, higher domestic interest rates and tax changes were creating challenges for customers. NAB employed 41,880 people globally as of September 30, 2025, according to its latest annual report. The move follows a similar restructuring drive at rival ANZ (ANZ.AX) , which last year announced plans to cut about [USN:L3N3UV1F1 TEXT:"3,500 jobs"] by September 2026 as part of a simplification program under CEO Nuno Matos to reduce duplication and lower costs. ($1 = 1.4329 Australian dollars)

item.title: Trading Day: AI storm abates
item.description: Wall Street recovered some ground on Monday as investors bought back beaten-down tech stocks and looked forward to key earnings reports, while easing worries over AI also cooled last week's safe-haven demand for bonds and pushed yields higher. Unrest and riots in France, meanwhile, weighed heavily on French bond prices and pushed the euro lower.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded:
[USN:L6N4650KA TEXT:"Wall Street"] recovered some ground on Monday as investors bought back beaten-down [USN:L4N4650VO TEXT:"tech stocks"] and looked forward to key earnings reports, while easing worries over AI also cooled last week's safe-haven demand for bonds and pushed yields higher. Unrest and riots in [USN:L1N4650EF TEXT:"France"], meanwhile, weighed heavily on French bond prices and pushed the euro lower. In [USN:L6N4620ZO TEXT:"my column today"], I look at AI's pivotal role in exacerbating global imbalances and driving global capital flows. The two are increasingly connected. If investor sentiment towards AI sours — and there are signs this may be happening — then the unwind could get messy. Today's Key Reads [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"France imposes curfews in parts of Paris, other cities after weekend of riots "] [USN:L1N46501H TEXT:"China's economic growth picks up as exports boom, consumers balk "] [USN:P8N42J00P TEXT:"China's central bank studies making overnight rate its main policy rate"] [USN:L4N45Z033 TEXT:"Global food inflation is expected to intensify as supply shocks pile up "] [USN:SPN46100U TEXT:"Ex-OpenAI employee accused of planting device appears to have Saudi backing, US prosecutors say"] Today's Key Market Moves STOCKS: Asia mostly higher, [USN:L4N464006 TEXT:"Indonesia "]-3.5%. [USN:L6N4650GG TEXT:"Europe"], [USN:L6N4650M4 TEXT:"UK "]slide around 1%. France -1%, although Italy and Spain fall more. Nasdaq +1.1%, S&P 500 +0.4%, Dow flat. SECTORS/SHARES: Four sectors on the S&P 500 rise, seven fall. Tech +1.2%, consumer cyclicals +2.7%. Utilities -2%. Western Digital +6%, Amazon +5%. JPMorgan Chase -2%. FX: Dollar rises vs most G10 except Aussie, [USN:L6N4650XD TEXT:"Canadian "]dollars. China's yuan hits four-year high vs dollar. BONDS: [USN:L6N4650CW TEXT:"French"] yields, spreads leap. US yields up around 3-4 bps across the curve. COMMODITIES/METALS: [USN:L4N464059 TEXT:"Oil"] mixed — Brent -0.5%, WTI +2%.

Today's Talking Points: Political risk sizzles [USN:L8N46401O TEXT:"France"], [USN:S8N442025 TEXT:"Brazil"], [USN:L1N4600TJ TEXT:"the US "]— just a few of the countries where polarized politics and looming elections are becoming increasingly important risk factors for investors to consider. France isn't the only country in Europe — or the world — facing unenviable fiscal challenges, but the riots spreading across the country are unlikely to make meeting them any easier. Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday in a closely contested runoff presidential election vote, and the US midterm elections barely two weeks away could see President Donald Trump's Republican Party lose control of both houses of Congress. Affordability, inflation, high energy prices, and worries over job security amid the AI revolution are issues dominating the national conversation in every country. Policymakers gathered in Bangkok for the IMF/World Bank meetings last week shared calls for fiscal discipline, AI vigilance, and tackling global trade imbalances. But that's easier said than done when domestic politics are so fractured everywhere, and the spirit of multilateralism is its lowest in decades. FXing a hole China's economy grew by 4.5% in the third quarter, official figures on Monday showed. The good news — that was faster than economists had expected; the not so good news — it was driven by roaring exports, which are putting the country on course to top last year's record $1.2 trillion trade surplus. China's bulging surplus is a key contributor to the expanding global imbalances that the IMF and others are warning about. Perhaps the rising yuan will help wean the economy off exports and support domestic demand. The yuan has been appreciating steadily for the last 18 months, and is now at a 4-year high against the dollar. But the yuan's broader 'real effective exchange rate,' or REER, is still on the weak side. Yes, its REER value has risen 7% since May last year, but it's also around 15% weaker than it was four years ago and right now is right on its average of the past 20 years. AI boomerang After last week's selloff, the global AI trade got off to a stronger start this week. At least, with tech earnings about to begin rolling out, sentiment in the US improved — the 'SOX' semiconductor index on Monday snapped an eight-day losing streak, its worst run since October 2008. The 2.5% rise on Monday is a good start, but there's more to go if last week's 11.5% slump is to be clawed back. Similarly, South Korea's KOSPI's 4% rebound in the last two trading sessions will be welcomed, but the index is still down around 20% from where it was two weeks ago. Like politics mentioned above, AI sentiment is becoming increasingly polarized. Few people doubt the technology's transformative significance, but bulls and bears are digging in for the long haul. All eyes are now on US earnings, and whether the incoming numbers and company outlooks justify the (still) lofty stock prices. What could move markets tomorrow? Euro zone current account (August) German ZEW index (October) German producer price inflation (September) UK employment (August) US earnings including GE Aerospace, Netflix, RTX. item.title: Ukraine's Zelenskiy says US decisions on Ukraine hard to explain
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that decisions taken by the United States on the war in Ukraine, including delays in arms shipments and restrictions on intelligence sharing, were "hard to explain."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that decisions taken by the United States on the war in Ukraine, including delays in arms shipments and restrictions on intelligence sharing, were "hard to explain." "Because it all comes down to (Russian President Vladimir) Putin's refusal to end this war , and to decisions on the American side that are hard to explain between friends," Zelenskiy said in a meeting with a US congressional delegation. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had not received full explanations over limitations placed on the use of the Starshield system needed to stage some drone strikes and defend against Russian attacks, particularly by high-speed jet-powered drones. In remarks posted on a video on Telegram, he said that on three occasions in the past week, Ukraine had not received the advance warning of an attack generally provided by its partners. "We also know that, unfortunately, the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles that our partner have already paid for through the PURL programme," he said. He said that to his knowledge one missile package was waiting for signature by US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. "All of this suggests that some political decision has been made to slow down support for us," he said. Zelenskiy also said that Ukraine was willing to halt strikes on Russian oil refineries, as demanded by US President Donald Trump , for 30 days if Washington supplied Ukraine with interceptors for the Patriot anti-missile system. He also said that he hoped a Ukrainian delegation would meet in the coming days with US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Norway.

item.title: Japan launches mission to return samples from Mars moon
item.description: Japan launched an uncrewed spacecraft toward the Martian moon Phobos on Tuesday on a mission intended to become the first to collect samples from the small rocky body and return them to Earth for analysis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan launched an uncrewed spacecraft toward the Martian moon Phobos on Tuesday on a mission intended to become the first to collect samples from the small rocky body and return them to Earth for analysis. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's Martian Moons eXploration spacecraft lifted off aboard an H3 rocket before dawn from the Tanegashima Space Center in southwestern Japan. The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars in August 2027 and return samples to Earth in 2031. JAXA hopes the mission will shed light on the origin of the two moons of Mars and deepen the understanding of our solar system's early stages. Phobos, the larger of the two Martian moons, orbits the planet three times a day. Phobos has an irregular shape with dimensions of about 27 km by 22 km by 18 km (17 miles by 14 miles by 11 miles), and orbits roughly 6,000 km (3,700 miles) above the Martian surface. JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grammes of material from its surface and return it to Earth for analysis. The launch marked the first interplanetary mission for Japan's H3 rocket. The country's flagship launcher experienced a high-profile failure on its inaugural flight in 2023 when its second-stage engine failed to ignite, but has since completed a series of mostly successful launches.

item.description:

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝ナスダック1％超高、半導体・ＡＩ株に買い戻し 5:12 配信

2026年10月8日、ニューヨーク証券取引所（NYSE）　 REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

［１９日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は、ハイテク株の比重が高いナスダック総合が１％超上昇した。先週大幅下落した半導体やその他の人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株に買いが戻った。投資家は主要企業の決算発表を待っている。

１６日までの週は、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が６月下旬以来の大幅な週間下落を記録した。金利上昇がＡＩインフラへの投資を抑制するとの懸念が、半導体企業やデータセンター運営会社を中心にハイテク株の重荷となってきた。

売りの背景には、多額の費用がかかるＡＩ開発の資金をどう調達するかを巡る投資家の不安の高まりがあった。この問題は、最近４周年を迎えた米国株の強気相場を支えてきた企業への圧力を強めている。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は１．６％高で引け、９営業日ぶりに反発した。それまでの８営業日で約１５．７％下落し、２００８年１０月以来の長期連続下落を記録していた。

ローゼンブラット・セキュリティーズのマネジングディレクター兼株式セールストレーダー、マイケル・ジェームズ氏は「ゴムひもは一方向に伸ばし続けても限界があり、やがて反動で逆方向に動き始める。１６日の取引終了後、半導体株ではようやく『もう十分だ』という転換点が訪れた」と指摘。

「１６日の引けから今朝の寄り付きまで、週末に悪材料が出なかったこと以外に何も変わっていない。投資家心理が極端に悪化し、反発してもおかしくないほど売られ過ぎていた」と語った。

その上で、今後数日から数週間に多くのハイテク企業の決算発表が予定されており、市場は「危機を脱したとは到底言えない」と警告した。

交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）大手メタ・プラットフォームズは０．５％安で終了した。同社は電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラとともに２１日に決算を発表する予定。スペースＸは２０日に発表する。

ダウ工業株３０種は小幅に下落、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種は小幅に上昇した。

ただ、相場の上昇は指数への影響が大きい大型株に強く依存した。また、主要指数は取引時間中にこの日の高値から水準を切り下げた。原油価格の変動に伴い、エネルギー市場からの支援材料が一部失われたことが一因だった。

米原油先物は序盤の下落から切り返し、２．２％高の１バレル＝１０３．６６ドルで清算した。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派がイエメンの軍事訓練施設を攻撃したほか、サウジアラビアのエネルギー施設や空港、軍事施設への攻撃を再開したことを受けた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種のうち７業種が下落した。一般消費財が２．７％高と上昇率首位で、情報技術が１．２％高と続いた。一方、ディフェンシブ業種の公益事業が２％安、不動産が１．２％安と、下落率が大きかった。

一般消費財を大きく押し上げたのはアマゾン・ドット・コムなどだった。モルガン・スタンレーが電子商取引とクラウドコンピューティングを手がける同社を「最有力推奨銘柄」に選定し、株価は５％高で終了した。テスラは３．８％上昇し、同業種指数への押し上げ寄与度が２番目に大きかった。

クラウドコンピューティング企業コアウィーブは、５００億ドルの債務負担への懸念から先週２５％超急落し、売りの中心となっていた。この日はゴールドマン・サックスによる投資判断の「ニュートラル」から「バイ」への引き上げに反応したとみられる序盤の上昇を維持できず、０．４％安で取引を終えた。

同業のネビウスは２．９％高、アイレンは２．７％高と、コアウィーブを上回る値動きとなった。インテルはＪＰモルガンが投資判断を「アンダーウエート」から「ニュートラル」に引き上げたことを受け、２．４％上昇した。

鉄鋼メーカーのクリーブランド・クリフスは、第３・四半期利益がアナリスト予想を上回り、１６％急伸した。

この日は、ダウ工業株３０種が１日の下落率として過去最大を記録した１９８７年の株価暴落「ブラックマンデー」から３９年に当たる。

ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）では、値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．６９対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでは値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．１７対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の合算出来高は１５２億７０００万株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７２億６０００万株。

Speaking alongside Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a red-c

Germany's Merz urges AI investment ahead of Nvidia deal

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz speak on stage during the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin, Germany, October 19, 2026. REUTERS/Lisi Niesner

FAST

BERLIN/FRANKFURT, Oct 19 : Chancellor Friedrich Merz appealed to Germany's businesses to embrace artificial intelligence at an industry summit in Berlin on Monday that was meant to attract investment, including an expected deal with US chip maker Nvidia.  Speaking alongside Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at a red-carpet event marking the start of the summit, Merz stressed the importance of AI in efforts to revive Germany's economy and modernise its industry.  Faced with global competition that is targeting the country's top auto, chemicals and engineering firms, Merz is under pressure to secure growth amid rising support for the far-right Alternative for Deutschland party.  "We are in the midst of a fundamental economic and technological transformation fuelled by exponential progress in artificial intelligence," Merz said, telling business leaders: "Please open your doors for AI to make use of your data."

Merz said cooperation with Nvidia was key for Germany's future success. Huang pointed to the company's existing cooperation with German carmakers like Mercedes-Benz, which is developing premium robotaxis using Nvidia software. Germany and Nvidia are expected to announce a partnership to promote AI in German industry at the summit, which continues on Tuesday. The German economy ministry has signed a memorandum of understanding with Nvidia, the government said, without giving further details. Huang also announced planned investments in German startups Agile Robots, Avelios Medical, Mirelo and Reflex Aerospace, Nvidia said in a blog post Monday. The investments are part of Nvidia's nearly $10 billion commitment to the technology ecosystem across Europe, it said. A German group of companies and investors that includes Siemens and Deutsche Bank said in a report that it sees the potential for investment of up to €4.1 trillion ($4.6 trillion) in Germany by 2035 across areas including AI, energy and defence. Made for Germany, a private sector business group, said its members planned to invest more than €850 billion through 2028, after investing more than €200 billion in 2025. More companies and investors have been invited to join the initiative. ($1 = €0.8926)

Source: Reuters

item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt, Ryan Patrick Jones
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Monday he is open to three-way arms-control talks with the leaders of China and Russia as soon as next month, raising the prospect of an unprecedented meeting and a major diplomatic gambit for the US president. "We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearization," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it. I'm sure we'd talk about other things like trade too." Trump has tried to thaw frosty relations with Beijing and Moscow as those non-Western powers grow closer. A three-way meeting would also raise alarm from Europe to Asia over private deals that weaken Washington's transatlantic and Indo-Pacific alliances. But a deal struck between the three countries could also lower global tensions. An end to Russia's war in Ukraine could resolve the biggest threat in decades to European security, and a deal on arms would bind the three nations with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons. In recent days, Trump has moved to warm ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin, announcing a diesel-fuel deal and signing an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow. Trump has also sought stable relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who in turn has nurtured close ties with Putin. So far, Trump has not delivered on a campaign promise to quickly end the war in Ukraine. The White House has been discussing for weeks a possible meeting between the leaders focused on denuclearization on the sidelines of the November 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, according to a person familiar with the matter. Putin later pitched using such a meeting to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict in a manner that would favor Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions. Putin's suggestion came during an October 9 phone call with Trump that yielded the deal on Russian diesel. Earlier on Monday, the Kremlin said that the potential meeting had come up in talks. The three leaders have met separately but never held formal talks together. The White House did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington also did not reply to requests for comment. Trump's diesel deal with Putin and the executive order waiving sanctions on Moscow have drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr [USN:L6N46517L TEXT:"Zelenskiy"], who has warned they would [USN:L1N4650WT TEXT:"embolden Putin"] and prolong the war. Speaking about the possible meeting on Monday, Trump said, "I would do it, not so much for Ukraine because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." He added that "Zelenskiy is not helping matters much," and that "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine." Moscow launched one of its [USN:L1N46500P TEXT:"broadest air assaults in months"] overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed. TRUMP SEEKS NUCLEAR TALKS Last week, Trump told reporters he thought a denuclearization deal with Russia and China was possible, but that it "doesn't have to be this year." It's not clear how advanced any talks between the countries are. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty [USN:FWN3Z10T1 TEXT:"expired"] earlier this year. The New START treaty, signed in 2010, allowed a single extension, which Putin and former US President Joe Biden agreed to for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty. China's foreign ministry said last week that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage." Trump has already agreed to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen next month, marking his second trip to China this year and his third visit with Xi over the same period. China, Russia and the United States are all members of APEC. On Monday, Trump downplayed the idea of another high-profile meeting in China, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. "I get along with him very well, and I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting," he said. Trump previously said he [USN:S0N41X02R TEXT:"planned to meet"] with Kim this year. North Korea has publicly indicated that it is not open to talks aimed at convincing Pyongyang to give up its nuclear weapons.

FAST

Oct 19 : Nscale is in talks to sell AI computing power to Claude maker Anthropic in a new deal that could be worth about $45 billion, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Monday. The data center developer is seeking another major deal with the AI lab for a second facility at its Monarch data center campus in West Virginia, the person said. In August, Anthropic struck a deal to spend $45 billion to rent AI cloud computing power from Nscale's West Virginia data center campus. A second Monarch building would deliver 460 megawatts of computing power using Nvidia's advanced Vera Rubin AI chips, according to the source. Anthropic did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Anthropic also has the right of first refusal on Monarch's expected third building, the person said, adding discussions were ongoing and details of the plan could change. Bloomberg, which first reported the news, also said a cohort of investors had urged Anthropic to lower its IPO valuation target after a series of market setbacks for AI companies. Investors have sharpened scrutiny of companies that are increasingly turning to debt-driven AI infrastructure expansion. Last week, Nscale rival CoreWeave's shares slumped amid concerns over its $50 billion debt load, fueling a global selloff in AI stocks. The news of a potential tie-up comes after Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor a flagship data center for Nscale following power connection delays that pushed its expected supply date into the 2030s. Nscale has grown rapidly since launch, increasing its total contracted value from $100 million to more than $103 billion in two-and-a-half years and competing with Nebius, Crusoe and Lambda. According to the Nscale prospectus, Microsoft and Anthropic are expected to be the company's major customers in the future.

Source: Reuters

item.description: ［ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ユーロが対ドルで下落した。フランスでの暴動が同...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ下落、仏財政懸念で　ドルはＡＩ株反発で上昇 4:35 配信

2026年10月19日、フランス・パリで撮影。REUTERS/Abdul Saboor

［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - 終盤のニューヨーク外為市場では、ユーロが対ドルで下落した。フランスでの暴動が同国の財政見通し悪化への懸念を一段と強めた。一方、ドルは人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の反発を受けて上昇した。

フランスでは、政府が財政赤字の縮小を図る中、政府に対する全国的な抗議デモが週末に暴動と略奪に発展。これを受け、フランス当局は１９日、首都パリや北部リール、南部ニースなど複数の都市の一部地域に夜間外出禁止令を発令した。

今回の暴動は、極右政党「国民連合（ＲＮ）」の実質的な指導者マリーヌ・ルペン氏が来年の大統領選で勝利する可能性を高めるとも見られており、フランスのＥＵ残留を巡って疑問が浮上する恐れがある。

ユーロは０．２４％安の１．１２１２ドル。独仏１０年債利回り格差は１４７ｂｐに拡大し、２０１１─１２年の欧州債務危機以来の水準で取引された。

主要通貨バスケットに対するドルの値動きを示すドル指数は０．１７％高の１０１．９７。

ドルは、ＡＩ関連株が先週の急落から反発したことを受けて上昇した。先週は、ＡＩ株に対する熱狂の後退が資本流入を細らせ、ドル需要を減退させるとの懸念からドルが押し下げられていた。

カナダドルは対米ドルで０．２７％高の１米ドル＝１．４１カナダドル。カナダ銀行（中銀）のマックレム総裁が１７日に示したタカ派的な発言が通貨を下支えした。

産油州であるアルバータ州では１９日、同州がカナダから分離独立すべきかどうかを問う住民投票が実施される。

円は対ドルで０．３５％下落し、１ドル＝１５８．４９円。

Famous Siberian cave yields remains of yak-like Ice Age mammal

A yak grazes on a grass patch some 3,000 metres (9,842 feet) above sea level in the mountains outside Almaty November 1, 2009. REUTERS/Shamil Zhumatov/File Photo

20 Oct 2026 02:52AM (Updated: 20 Oct 2026 02:54AM)

FAST

Oct 19 : A Siberian cave already famous for yielding the first remains of an extinct human lineage called the Denisovans, who once roamed widely in Eurasia, has now produced evidence of a previously unknown large Ice Age mammal closely related to today's yak. Researchers said they discovered small bone fragments of the animal in Denisova Cave in the Altai Mountains of southern Siberia in Russia, and obtained DNA that showed these remains belonged to a bovine species distinct from others already known, living and extinct. In all, the researchers studied 20 bone fragments from this species — 14 from Denisova Cave and 6 from other sites in the broader region. The oldest specimen dated to about 250,000 to 200,000 years ago, and the youngest to about 27,000 years ago. The bones themselves were so fragmentary that their shape alone did not reveal that they belonged to a previously unknown large mammal. But the researchers were able to generate 20 ancient genomes from the bones, and these showed that this was a unique species whose evolutionary lineage diverged from the ancestors of the modern-day yak approximately 400,000 years ago.

"It is unusual, especially to recognize a large mammal species from small, unidentifiable fragments," said evolutionary geneticist Love Dalén of the Centre for Palaeogenetics, a collaboration between Stockholm University and the Swedish Museum of Natural History, senior author of the research published in the journal Current Biology. "I'd say that this is related to the advances in the field of ancient DNA, as genetics is a powerful new layer of information applied to ancient materials," said Alexandre Gilardet, a doctoral student at the Centre for Palaeogenetics and co-lead author of the study, along with Centre for Palaeogenetics postdoctoral researcher Jonas Oppenheimer. Genetic evidence alone is not sufficient to allow for giving a scientific name to a new species, so the researchers are calling this one "Yak X." THE ICE AGE LANDSCAPE Dalén said Yak X lived alongside other bovines including steppe bison and the aurochs, the extinct wild ancestor of today's domesticated cattle. It also shared the Ice Age landscape with woolly mammoths, woolly rhinoceroses, horses and large predators such as cave hyenas and brown bears, Dalén said. "I'd expect it to have looked more like a yak than a bison, given its close relationship to modern yaks," Dalén said. Yaks are sturdily built animals with horns, long fur and a hump at the shoulders, looking a bit like a hairy ox. The largest males can weigh as much as a ton. Wild yaks are restricted to higher elevations of the Tibetan Plateau. The Yak X discovery deepens the understanding of the diversity of large Ice Age mammals and adds another species to the long list that disappeared at around the end of that epoch. "Using the long, 200,000-year time span of our sampling, we can see that the species may have undergone a population decline during a period of warming around 120,000 years ago, and went extinct some time after our youngest sample, about 27,000 years ago," Oppenheimer said. The vast Siberian expanse was a grassland ecosystem called the mammoth steppe, known as such for its largest denizens. Most of the region was left uncovered by the immense ice sheets that had blanketed large swathes of North America and Europe. The Yak X lineage diverged from the ancestors of modern yaks around the same time as the evolutionary split that occurred between the ursine lineages that led to today's brown bears and polar bears. THE DENISOVANS It was in Denisova Cave in 2008 that scientists unearthed a finger bone that offered the first evidence of the existence of Denisovans, extinct cousins of Neanderthals and our own species, Homo sapiens. Since then, more remains of Denisovans have been discovered in the cave and in several far-flung parts of Asia. Some modern populations of people, especially those in Melanesia and Papua New Guinea, carry a small percentage of DNA from Denisovans, indicating interbreeding with Homo sapiens before the Denisovans became extinct under circumstances that are not well understood. Denisovans were hunter-gatherers who survived in many different types of environments. The Yak X species might have been among the prey that they hunted. "It seems reasonable that Yak X was on the Denisovan menu," Dalén said.

Source: Reuters

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（19日） 3:50 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

反落して取引を終えた。銀行や鉱業株が売られ、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は４営業日ぶりに反落した。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．６３％安と、７営業日ぶりの反落。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は２．３３％安。銀行大手のバークレイズは３．５％下落。プライベートクレジット融資に関する流動性などのリスクを過小評価するような不適切な表示をした疑いでイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）が調査していると伝わった。

鉱業株指数は２．６５％安。銅価格の値下がりを受けて、資源大手アングロ・アメリカンは４．１％、グレンコアは３．３％、それぞれ下落した。

航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．３７％、公益事業株指数は２．１３％、それぞれ値下がりした。通期生産見通しを引き下げた石油・ガス会社セリカ・エナジーは２．０％下落した。

ヒーリー英財務相による初の予算案公表を来週に控える中、今週は消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）や小売売上高といった英経済指標が発表される。多くの企業決算も開示される予定となっている。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

４営業日ぶりに反落して取引を終えた。２０２７年に大統領選を控えるフランスで、物価高や公共サービスの悪化に抗議するデモが拡大し、政局が混迷しつつある。財政を巡る懸念も相場の重荷となり、フランスのＣＡＣ４０指数は１．１１％下落した。このほか、総選挙を１１月に控えて政治的な不透明感が強まったスペインのＩＢＥＸ指数も１．４９％安だった。

フランスの金融機関ＢＮＰパリバ、クレディ・アグリコル、ソシエテ・ジェネラルは２．５─３．４％下落。フランスの小売大手カルフールは２．２％、ショッピングセンターなどを手がけるウニベイル・ロダムコ・ウエストフィールドは２．１％それぞれ値下がりした。

ＳＴＯＸＸユーロ圏銀行株指数は２．０７％下落。ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．４３％安。

一方、テクノロジー株指数は０．７０％上昇。

今週は、ドイツのソフトウエア大手ＳＡＰ、フィンランドの通信機器大手ノキア、英銀大手のバークレイズの決算発表が予定されている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

フランス国債利回りが上昇した。週末にフランス全土で抗議活動が繰り広げられたことを受け、巨額の財政赤字削減が同国政府にとっていかに困難かが浮き彫りとなった。

フランスでは１７日、生活費の高騰と公共サービスの質の低下に抗議するデモが一部で暴徒化し、同国で過去数十年で最大規模の暴動に発展。商業・小売連盟によると、週末に被害を受けた店舗は約３０００店に上っている。

投資家は、フランスが財政を立て直すには予算案を可決する必要があると指摘しているが、今回の抗議デモはそれがいかに難しいかを示している。来年の大統領選を控えた政治的な駆け引きが、事態をさらに複雑にする可能性もある。

ＳＭＢＣのグローバル市場ストラテジスト、ハンク・カレンティ氏は、財政赤字削減や年金改革の取り組みに言及し「抗議デモが繰り広げられた週末を経てこうした動きになったことは、改革への期待が後退していることを示している」と述べた。

フランス１０年債利回りは１３ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の４．９％と、１日としては９月下旬以来の上昇幅となる見通しとなった。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは４ｂｐ上昇の３．４５％。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１４６ｂｐと、２週間ぶりの高水準となった。それでも、１０月序盤に付けた１６０ｂｐ近辺からは縮小している。

イタリア１０年債利回りは１１ｂｐ上昇の４．５８％。

item.title: Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil asks US Supreme Court to hear case seeking to avoid re-arrest
item.description: Columbia University graduate Mahmoud Khalil on Monday asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that opened the door for President Donald Trump's administration to re-arrest and deport the Palestinian activist.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond, Jonathan Allen
item.content:encoded: Columbia University graduate [USN:L1N3SG0OI TEXT:"Mahmoud Khalil"] on Monday asked the US Supreme Court to overturn a ruling that opened the door for President Donald Trump's administration to re-arrest and deport the Palestinian activist. Khalil's lawyers asked the justices to take up his case after the Philadelphia-based 3rd US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that federal immigration law barred a lower-court judge from ordering his release from US Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody. Khalil was among the most prominent foreign students to be arrested last year as the Trump administration pursued a campaign to detain and deport noncitizens who engaged in pro-Palestinian activism on college campuses. His lawyers say the Supreme Court should make clear immigration law does not prevent noncitizens from pursuing cases arguing they have been detained to punish them for speech that is protected by the US Constitution's First Amendment. "If the Trump administration can punish someone for their pro-Palestine speech, this or any future administration can punish anyone for any speech," Khalil told reporters on Monday. If the 3rd Circuit's decision is allowed to stand, Khalil faces the prospect of arrest and deportation, after the Board of Immigration Appeals in April rejected his challenge to an immigration judge's order that he be removed to Algeria or Syria. A lower court order barring him from being re-detained remains in place for now until the Supreme Court rules. A separate appeal of the immigration judge's order remains pending. A spokesperson for the US Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, in a statement said the Trump administration acted within its authority in Khalil's case, and it encouraged him to self-deport. KHALIL'S BACKGROUND AND ARREST Khalil, a prominent figure in pro-Palestinian protests against Israel's war in Gaza , is an Algerian citizen who was born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria. Immigration agents arrested him in March 2025 in the lobby of his university residence in Manhattan despite his being a lawful permanent resident, or green-card holder. His wife and their 1-year-old son are both US citizens. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had invoked an obscure provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act to deem Khalil removable, citing his involvement in "antisemitic protests and disruptive activities" at Columbia in 2024 that the government said fostered a hostile environment for Jewish students. He was released from a Louisiana detention center in June 2025 after the New Jersey-based US District Judge Michael Farbiarz, an appointee of former President Joe Biden, ordered the Department of Homeland Security to release him. In January, a 2-1 panel of the 3rd Circuit overturned Farbiarz's decision, saying that under the Immigration and Nationality Act, Khalil's claims could not be addressed through a district court and instead could be raised in an appeal of a removal order from an immigration judge. After the full appeals court declined to reconsider the case, Khalil turned to the Supreme Court. Federal appeals courts are split on whether district judges may hear challenges like Khalil's or whether such claims must proceed first through immigration courts, which are not part of the federal judiciary but are instead run by the US Department of Justice. The Trump administration [USN:L1N45E0AE TEXT:"last month asked"] the Supreme Court to overturn a ruling in a similar case favoring Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri, another pro-Palestinian advocate detained by ICE who was ordered released.

MUMBAI, Oct 19 : Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance said on Monday that Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity were among investors who bid in the anchor book of its record $3.2 billion Jio Platforms IPO, which two sources said drew more than $25 billion in demand. The telecoms, cloud and AI group on Monday opened its record initial public offering to institutional investors who can bid for up to 30 per cent of the offering exclusively earmarked for them, before the issue opens for public subscription on Wednesday.  Jio Platforms allocated shares worth over 81 billion rupees ($853.31 million) to anchor investors, a company filing showed on Monday. State-run insurer Life Insurance Corporation, French lender BNP Paribas, JPMorgan, India's largest private-sector lender HDFC Bank were among the other institutions allotted shares in the IPO anchor book.

The bids drawn were over 30 times the quota reserved for anchor investors, a source told Reuters. Jio upended India's telecoms market in 2016 by offering free voice calls and cheap data and soon became the country's biggest mobile operator. It now has more than 500 million subscribers and competes with Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea. Its listing is seen as a test of what global investors will pay for that scale and for Jio's expansion into cloud and AI. Led by Mukesh Ambani's son Akash Ambani, Jio operates Reliance Industries' telecom and digital businesses, spanning mobile services, fixed broadband, cloud, entertainment, enterprise technology and AI offerings. Jio's IPO follows September's listing of the National Stock Exchange of India, underscoring investor appetite for large offerings in the Indian market. It will be the first offering by Reliance since its listing of Reliance Petroleum in 2006. Year-to-date Indian IPO proceeds rose 8.3 per cent to $12.65 billion compared with the same period last year, LSEG data shows. A successful IPO would place Jio Platforms among the top four Indian listed companies by market capitalisation, behind its parent Reliance, its rival Bharti Airtel and the country's largest private lender HDFC Bank. Jio plans to use up to 275 billion Indian rupees ($2.90 billion) of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings of its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm. ($1 = 94.9475 Indian rupees)

Source: Reuters

The company said on Thursday content chief Bela Bajaria would leave after nearly a decade with the streaming platform, and would be replaced by former Disney executive Peter Rice. • Rice will oversee the films division until a new head is announced • Netflix's growth prospects and user engagement are under scrutiny; its co-CEO Ted Sarandos recently said the company is "not growing as fast as I want us to"

item.title: Brazil's government says $4 billion budget reshuffle needed for Lula measures in 2027
item.description: Brazil's Planning Ministry said on Monday that the budget reallocations needed to accommodate measures recently announced by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as he seeks re-election in next Sunday's vote amount to about 20 billion reais ($3.95 billion) in the 2027 budget.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazil's Planning Ministry said on Monday that the budget reallocations needed to accommodate measures recently announced by President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as he seeks re-election in next Sunday's vote amount to about 20 billion reais ($3.95 billion) in the 2027 budget. In a statement, the ministry said the amount represents just over 1% of total primary expenditure subject to spending limits under Brazil's fiscal framework, adding such adjustments will be made while preserving both the overall spending cap and the government's primary [USN:L1N44S10B TEXT:"budget target"]. Leftist Lula has unveiled a string of measures ahead of Sunday's runoff after [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"trailing"] right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in the first round Announcements [USN:L1N46114S TEXT:"range"] from free nationwide weekend public transport, which has yet to be formally submitted to Congress, to a 15% increase in the Bolsa Familia welfare program that is already being implemented The government said the Bolsa Familia increase alone would [USN:L1N4590JP TEXT:"cost"] 22 billion reais in 2027 The Planning Ministry did not explain how the budget reallocations required to fund the broader package of measures would amount to less than that The ministry said estimates circulating publicly about the total fiscal impact wrongly combine measures with different funding sources and implementation timelines, arguing some policies, such as fuel tax relief, have been offset by higher oil-related revenue It added that public policy implementation should not automatically be viewed as election-driven spending ($1 = 5.0612 reais)

item.title: Ronaldo handed 30-day ban for leaving Portugal camp following coach Jesus rift
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese FA on Monday after leaving the national team camp following a rift with coach Jorge Jesus over his role in the side.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cristiano Ronaldo was suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese FA on Monday after [USN:L6N45M14A TEXT:"leaving"] the national team camp following a [USN:L6N45M14A TEXT:"rift"] with coach Jorge Jesus over his role in the side. The federation's disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of 255 euros ($285.83). Ronaldo left Portugal's base in Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark earlier this month, having accused Jesus of twice breaking his word about his role after he was an unused substitute against Norway. Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return following Portugal's 2-1 win. The disciplinary council's non-professional section found Ronaldo had intentionally committed an offence under Article 160(1) of the federation's disciplinary regulations. Proceedings were opened on October 9 over facts reported two days earlier. The statement did not specify which matches or activities the suspension would cover, or whether time already served under a provisional suspension would count towards the 30-day sanction. Ronaldo later apologised for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match and for leaving his teammates, saying he remained available for selection after serving any punishment arising from the incident. Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca has said everyone within the federation wanted Ronaldo to return to the national team once the matter was resolved. ($1 = 0.8921 euros)

NEW YORK, Oct 19 : IT services company DXC Technology is in advanced talks to sell its insurance software and services division to private investment firm Eldridge Industries for about $2.4 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Eldridge is discussing combining the business with Zinnia, its insurance technology platform that provides software and digital infrastructure to life insurance and annuity providers, the sources said. An agreement could be reached in the coming weeks, although there is no certainty a deal will be finalized, the people said, requesting anonymity because the discussions are confidential. DXC Technology, Eldridge and Zinnia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The transaction would mark a significant divestiture for DXC as the information technology services provider seeks to streamline its portfolio after several years of declining revenue.  The sale would allow DXC to exit a business that provides technology and outsourcing services to insurers globally, helping the IT services provider streamline its operations after several years of declining revenue. Its insurance division offers policy administration systems and other software and business process services to insurers across life, wealth, property and casualty markets.  For Eldridge, a transaction would combine Zinnia's life and annuity technology platform with DXC Technology's insurance software and business-process services operations, creating a scaled provider of software, administration and servicing technology for insurers.

item.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader convicted of deaths of nearly 200 children
item.description: Starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and 28 others were found guilty of murder by a Kenyan court on Monday over the deaths of 190 children and an adult in one of the world's worst cult-related tragedies in recent history.
item.dc:creator: Jefferson Kahinju
item.content:encoded: Starvation [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"cult leader Paul Mackenzie"] and 28 others were found guilty of murder by a Kenyan court on Monday over the deaths of 190 children and an adult in one of the world's worst cult-related tragedies in recent history. The preacher was [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"arrested in 2023"] after police received a tip-off, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola Forest near the coast in southeastern Kenya. Prosecutors say Mackenzie and his Good News International Church organised a Christian doomsday sect in which they ordered followers to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. The case has gripped Kenya since the discovery of the mass graves. It raised questions over how Mackenzie was able to continue to operate despite having been on the radar of the authorities since 2017 when his premises were searched by police. In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie's church and he relocated to the Shakahola Forest, police said. GRANDFATHER HAILS JUDGMENT Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve, but the court rejected that argument. He and the others convicted will be sentenced on November 6. Defence lawyer Lawrence Obonyo, who represents Mackenzie and almost all of the others convicted, said he had been instructed to appeal. Francis Wanje, 62, lost eight family members including two grandchildren to the cult. He told Reuters that the judgment made him happy and gave him confidence in the judiciary. "So many are going to learn from what has come up today. ... You find churches everywhere, but they've got ill reasons for the churches. So it is good for members of the public to be very careful," Wanje added. HEARING LASTED MORE THAN EIGHT HOURS In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered from the Shakahola Forest. Many of the children's bodies were severely decomposed, with only 26 able to be identified, and investigations into the other deaths are ongoing. Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched. The director of public prosecutions, Renson Ingonga, told reporters afterwards at the Mombasa High Court: "That is the best judgment we would ever get." MACKENZIE SILENT WHEN JUDGE CALLED HIM BY NAME Mackenzie was in court, wearing a striped polo shirt and red trousers, sitting alongside his wife, one of the co-accused. When his name was read out by the judge he was silent, staring into space. The case has led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life. Kenyan President William Ruto said in 2023 that government agencies should have been able to prevent the deaths. He said he took responsibility as president. CHILDREN WERE FIRST TO STARVE People with direct knowledge of the cult's activities have [USN:L8N36W0BR TEXT:"told Reuters"] that Mackenzie planned the mass starvation in three phases: first children, then women and young men, and finally the remaining men. A former taxi driver, Mackenzie forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, branding such institutions as satanic, relatives of some of his victims told Reuters for a 2023 article. Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names like Jerusalem and Judea. The plight of his followers began to emerge in mid-March 2023, when a local man told police that his brother and wife had starved their children to death in the forest on Mackenzie's orders. Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives say he brought forward the date on which he told his followers the world would end. Police arrested him again in April 2023 and started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves. Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths including terrorism-related ones, which he has denied. Prosecutors say while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in [USN:L8N3Z51Y2 TEXT:"Kwa Binzaro village"], which lies about 30 km (18 miles) from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.

item.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts has blood clots in lungs, out for season
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs, the team announced Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed blood clots in his lungs, the team announced Monday. Hurts' condition is considered stable and he "has no significant functional limitations," the team said. His treatment for a new diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli will involve blood thinners, during which time he is unable to participate in contact activities. The 28-year-old veteran's prognosis is good and the team said it expects a full recovery with no long-term effects. Specialists in London initially diagnosed a superficial blood clot in Hurts' left calf on Oct. 10, the day before Philadelphia's 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Further testing discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners," the team's statement concluded. "In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects." Regarding the decision to play Hurts in London, even though they reportedly were aware of the blood clot before the game. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said Monday regarding that decision, "(I) leave that up to the medical experts, but we always, always care deeply about our players. And that's when you are completely focused on together and connection. You're always thinking about the well-being of your guys and that's what we were in that situation. ... "I'm not a medical expert. I lean on our guys in all those situations, right? I'm a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every situation. I have full trust and full faith in them." Sirianni declined to reveal the substance of his latest conversation with Hurts after learning that the QB was out for the year, though he did say, "I just deeply care about him and hope that he continues to improve with what he's going through." Hurts, a three-time Pro Bowl selection and the MVP of Super Bowl LIX, has compiled a 59-28 regular-season record since taking over as the starter late in his rookie season in 2020. He has passed for 18,824 yards with 118 touchdowns and 48 interceptions and rushed for 3,661 yards and 64 touchdowns. Hurts completed 57.8% of his passes for 933 yards, eight TDs and three interceptions in five starts (2-3 record) this season. Backup Tanner McKee started in Hurts' place on Sunday as the Eagles (2-4) sustained their fourth consecutive loss, a 25-14 setback at home to the Carolina Panthers. "I have the utmost confidence in Tanner," Sirianni said Monday. --Field Level Media

item.title: 米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準 ローン金利・建材高が重し
item.description: [ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米住宅建設業者指数、10月は約14年半ぶり低水準　ローン金利・建材高が重し 10/19 23:47 配信

米カリフォルニア州エンシニタスにある一戸建て住宅。８月撮影。REUTERS/Mike Blake

[ワシントン １９日 ロイター] - 全米住宅建設業協会（ＮＡＨＢ）が１９日発表した１０月のＮＡＨＢ／ウェルズ・ファーゴ住宅建設業者指数は２９と、前月の３２から低下し、２０１２年６月以来、約１４年半ぶりの低水準となった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は３１への低下だった。

中東紛争により住宅ローン金利とエネルギー関連の建材価格が上昇しているほか、移民取り締まりに伴う人手不足や、関税措置によるコスト上昇が影響している。

住宅ローン金利はここ数週間で急上昇しており、住宅金融公社フレディマックのデータによると、３０年固定住宅ローン金利は先週、７．４０％と約３年ぶりの高水準となった。米国とイスラエルの対イラン戦争がインフレをあおる中、米国債利回りに連動して借り入れコストが上昇し、住宅販売を圧迫している。

ＮＡＨＢのビル・オーウェンズ会長は「住宅建設業者は、建設ローンや建築建材、ディーゼル燃料のコスト上昇に加え、慢性的な人手不足にも直面している」と指摘。「全米で建設業者の３分の１超が、過去１カ月間に自社の事業地域で移民取り締まりの動きがあったと報告しており、これが建設の遅れや、合法的な労働者が出勤を躊躇（ちゅうちょ）する事態を招いている」と述べた。

買い手を呼び込むために値下げを実施した建設業者は４３％と、２０─２６年の期間で最も高い割合となった。平均値下げ幅は６％と横ばいだった。販売促進策の実施率は６５％。１９カ月連続で６０％以上となっている。

現在の販売状況を示す指数は２ポイント低下の３３。販売見通しを示す指数は５ポイント低下の３２となった。

見込み客の来場状況を示す指数は５ポイント低下の１８。ＮＡＨＢのチーフエコノミスト、ロバート・ディーツ氏は同指数について、コロナ禍の２０年４月を除くと、１２年４月以来の低水準だと指摘した。

item.description: ［ニューヨーク １９日 ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場・午前＝Ｓ＆Ｐ・ナスダック上昇、ＡＩ関連が反発 10/19 23:33 配信

2026年7月20日に撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

［ニューヨーク　１９日　ロイター］ - １９日午前の米国株式市場では、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が上昇した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株が前週の急落から反発したほか、原油価格の下落も支援材料となった。ナスダック総合指数は一時２５５．３ポイント（０．９８％）上昇した。

人工知能（ＡＩ）向けクラウドサービスを手がけるコアウィーブは、投資判断の引き上げを受けて３．４％高と急伸した。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、同社の投資判断を「中立」から「買い」に引き上げた。コンピューティング能力の供給が逼迫していることや、競合企業に対する業績面での優位性から、今後２年間でメガワット当たりの年間経常収益が押し上げられるはずだとし、直近の下落は買いの好機だとした。前週には、同社の抱える５００億ドルの債務を巡る懸念がＡＩセクター全体に広がり、株価の４分の１超を失っていた。

競合のネビウス・グループは４．５％高。過去２週間で３１％超下落していた。データセンター運営のアプライド・デジタルは９％、ＩＲＥＮは５．７％、それぞれ上昇した。

フィラデルフィア半導体指数は２．８％高で推移。前週に１１％超下落し、ＡＩ関連の急落局面で最も打撃を受けた銘柄群の一つとなった。

インテルは５．６％上昇した。ＪＰモルガンが投資判断を「アンダーウエート」から「ニュートラル」に引き上げたことが材料となった。

エヌビディアは０．６％、ＡＭＤは４．３％、ブロードコムは２．２％、それぞれ上昇した。３社とも前週に大きく売られていた。

マイクロン・テクノロジーは３．８％高。前週には約１５％下落していた。データストレージのサンディスク、ウエスタン・デジタル、シーゲイトも前週の大幅安から反発した。

item.title: India probing Pernod, Diageo Scotch imports under India-UK trade pact, sources say
item.description: Indian tax officials are investigating whether liquor giants Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified some bulk Scotch imports, allowing them to pay lower tariffs introduced under the recently agreed India-UK trade pact, five industry sources familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: Indian tax officials are investigating whether liquor giants Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) and Diageo (DGE.L) wrongly classified some bulk Scotch imports, allowing them to pay lower tariffs introduced under the recently agreed India-UK trade pact, five industry sources familiar with the matter said. Import tariff disputes have long been a [USN:L4N3P10W5 TEXT:"sore point"] for foreign investors in India and embroiled companies like [USN:L4N45E0CD TEXT:"Samsung"], LG and Volkswagen. They often involve large back-tax demands raised years after the items were imported, with Indian officials saying they are only enforcing the law. Last week, tax inspectors made an unexpected visit to Pernod's India headquarters near New Delhi where they questioned company executives about their Scotch imports, three of the people said. Diageo's Indian unit, United Spirits (UNSP.NS) , in a stock exchange filing last week said its offices in multiple locations were searched on Friday as part of an "industry-wide exercise" by authorities, without saying what the search related to. The other two people said Diageo is also being investigated for how it classifies some Scotch imports. Pernod (PERP.PA) told Reuters in a statement that it is cooperating with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and providing all information requested, adding it was committed to addressing any questions from the authorities. Diageo (DGE.L) , also in a statement, said it is cooperating with Indian authorities, and has always complied with local laws. In its stock exchange disclosure, it said it had provided all documents and clarifications. The Indian revenue directorate did not respond to a request for comment. Reuters is first to report that tax inspectors visited Pernod's India office, and publish details of the probe, including that it is linked to the UK-India tariff declarations. BULK SCOTCH IMPORTS Diageo and France's Pernod Ricard dominate India’s $65 billion alcohol market. Both companies import bulk Scotch concentrates in containers to mix with other ingredients to make brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell’s. Under the [USN:L4N43H0E5 TEXT:"trade pact"], which took effect on July 15, India agreed to slash import taxes on certain Scotch imports to 75%, from 150%. The tax inspectors argued that the duty relief did not apply to bulk concentrates, four of the people said. "The tax department is concerned that bulk imports are being wrongly classified," one of them said. ICONIC PRODUCT The UK accounts for almost 75% of India's imported spirits market, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, Crisil Ratings said this year. In July, the British government said "iconic UK products" including whiskies and gin would benefit from India's tariff changes. It added that the UK's whisky exports to the country were worth more than £200 million in 2022. Pernod is already facing antitrust cases in India, its biggest market by volume, and a [USN:L4N41Z12U TEXT:"$314 million"] back-tax demand for allegedly undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing. Diageo in August agreed to [USN:L4N44E10L TEXT:"reformulate"] some of its most popular drinks after the country's food safety regulator banned them in some states for adding flavours against regulations. During the visit to Pernod's India office on Thursday, tax inspectors reviewed some documents related to bulk Scotch imports, but have not been in contact since, said one of the people.

item.title: Qatari electricity lifeline for Lebanon includes two power plants, LNG supply deal
item.description: Qatar plans to construct two power plants in Lebanon over the next three years and sign a 20-year liquefied natural gas supply deal under a proposal to revive the ailing Lebanese power sector, a document seen by Reuters showed.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Qatar plans to construct two power plants in Lebanon over the next three years and sign a 20-year liquefied natural gas supply deal under a proposal to revive the ailing Lebanese power sector, a document seen by Reuters showed. Lebanon's energy sector is at the centre of the country's financial and economic malaise, contributing tens of billions of dollars to the national debt since the country's 1975-1990 civil war even as it failed to deliver 24/7 power. The state power company currently supplies just a few hours of power per day, with the rest coming from expensive private diesel generators that spew toxic exhaust often seen forming a yellow-grey layer of smog above Beirut. Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani visited Lebanon last week and publicly promised to help revitalise the country's power sector. Few details were then presented to reporters. But according to a proposal drafted with input from the Lebanese and Qatari governments, dated October 2026 and seen by Reuters, the programme "covers gas-fired power generation, LNG supply and regasification, renewable energy, battery storage, and regional electricity interconnections". "The program aims to attract private/project financing without upfront Lebanese public-budget capital expenditure; payment obligations and guarantees remain subject to negotiation," the document said. The blueprint, named the National Integrated Energy Investment Program, still requires the approval of both governments and is subject to amendment, a person familiar with the matter said. They put the timeframe for implementation at three years if approvals come swiftly. Qatar has been a longtime financial and political backer of Lebanon, stepping in multiple times over the last decades during times of political and economic crisis. The Qatari Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the proposed plan. Lebanon's energy minister also did not respond to a request for comment. PROPOSAL FOLLOWS GROWING QATARI PRESENCE IN SYRIA According to the document, the plan includes two new combined-cycle plants at Deir Ammar in northern Lebanon and at Zahrani in the south, each at a capacity of 825 megawatts. QatarEnergy would also enter a 20-year LNG supply agreement with Lebanon, using both a floating storage and regasification unit with a capacity of 3.5 million cubic meters per day, and the Arab Gas Pipeline via Syria at a capacity of 4.5 million cubic meters per day. The proposal also includes plans for 800 MW of solar and 440 MW of wind, battery capacity and power imports from Syria, beginning with 300 MW via two separate routes. Numerous proposals to reform Lebanon's power sector and provide electricity through the national grid have repeatedly stalled due to political bickering and the vested interests of senior politicians in the fuel and energy sectors. The proposal would build on a growing Qatari presence in neighbouring Syria, where Qatari conglomerate Power International Holding has secured contracts for 5,000 MW of power generation, as well as oil and gas extraction and pipelines.

item.title: US Supreme Court will not review Trump's firing of labor board member
item.description: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by a Democratic-appointed member of the National Labor Relations Board to challenge the legality of her firing by President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by a Democratic-appointed member of the National Labor Relations Board to challenge the legality of her firing by President Donald Trump . The justices turned away former NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox's appeal of a lower court's ruling that said the Republican president's January 2025 firing of her was a valid exercise of executive authority. The court's action follows its June decision [USN:S0N3YR013 TEXT:"backing Trump's firing"] of Rebecca Slaughter, a Democratic Federal Trade Commission member. That ruling overturned the court's 1935 precedent in a case called Humphrey's Executor that had recognized the authority of Congress to protect leaders of certain regulatory agencies from presidential removal at will. The Slaughter decision capped a decades-long conservative push to strengthen the president's grip on key levers of government power. Trump's move to oust Wilcox from the NLRB was part of his shakeup and downsizing of the US government, including firing thousands of workers, dismantling federal agencies, installing loyalists in key jobs and purging career officials. "I'm disappointed that the Supreme Court has declined to hear this case, not only for myself, but also for the workers and employers who rely on the National Labor Relations Board to resolve labor disputes impartially and free from political pressure," Wilcox said in a statement. Wilcox added that she would remain committed to "protecting the principles that allow the board to serve the public fairly." The Justice Department declined to comment. Wilcox, the first Black woman to serve on the agency's board, was appointed to a second five-year term in 2023 by Democratic former President Joe Biden. Trump moved to fire her about a week into his second presidential term, drawing a lawsuit by Wilcox. Slaughter also was a Biden appointee. The legal fight over Trump's firing of Wilcox and other officials has figured as a key test of his efforts to bring federal agencies meant by Congress to be independent from the president under his control. US District Judge Beryl Howell in March 2025 upheld a federal law protecting NLRB officials from being fired without cause, rejecting Trump's argument that the measure passed by Congress encroaches on authority granted to the president under the US Constitution. That ruling was reversed in a 2-1 decision by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit in December 2025, prompting Wilcox's appeal to the Supreme Court.

item.title: ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求 市場改革も表明
item.description:
Ankur Banerjee Stefanno Sulaiman
[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ジャカルタ株が過去2日で最大の下落、ＭＳＣＩに説明要求　市場改革も表明 10/19 22:13 配信

株価ボード、ジャカルタのインドネシア証券取引所で16日撮影 REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana/File Photo

Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ １９日 ロイター] - インドネシア株式市場は１９日、２営業日の下落としては過去最大を記録した。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが１６日、２０２７年に同国を「新興国市場」から除外する可能性を警告したことが売りを誘発。当局はＭＳＣＩに説明を求めた。

ジャカルタ総合指数は１６日に１１．６％急落したのに続き、１９日は３．６％安で取引を終えた。２営業日の下落率は１９９８年のアジア金融危機時を含め過去最大となった。取引時間中には６年ぶりの安値も付けた。

ＭＳＣＩが１６日、インドネシアを「新興国市場」から「スタンドアローン市場」に変更することを検討していると表明したことで売りが始まった。想定以上に厳しい分類変更の可能性に、投資家や当局者に動揺が広がった。

スタンドアローン市場に変更されれば、東南アジア最大の経済規模を持つインドネシアは国際資本へのアクセスを失い、投資先として周縁に追いやられる恐れがある。

不安心理からの売りは通貨や債券市場にも波及した。ルピアは１ドル＝１万８０３０ルピアに下落、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに迫った。国債も下落し、１０年債利回りは１６日の７．１６９％から７．４％に上昇した。

インドネシア証券取引所のジェフリー・ヘンドリック最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は、説明を求めるためのＭＳＣＩとの会合を前に「（ＭＳＣＩから）このような発表があるとは予想していなかった。予想外の声明で市場はパニックに陥った」と述べた。

＜資本市場改革への取り組み継続＞

ヘンドリック氏はＭＳＣＩとのオンライン会合後、１月にＭＳＣＩが最初の警告を発したことを受けて着手した資本市場改革に引き続き取り組むと述べた。会合の詳細は明らかにできないとした。

同氏はまた、市場の透明性と価格発見機能を改善するための２つの施策を発表した。同一の個人や法人に株式保有が高度に集中している銘柄をジャカルタ総合指数から除外する措置が含まれる。「主要指数の動きをより正確に示す」ことが狙いという。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、価格変動の抑制に向け、株価の１日の下落率の上限を１５％から７％に縮小した。それを下回る価格での売り注文を自動的に拒否し、一段の下落を防ぐ。

＜投資家、インドネシア資産への投資を再評価＞

ＭＳＣＩの動きを受け、投資家がインドネシア資産全般への投資を見直す中、規制当局や財政・金融当局への圧力が強まっている。

かつて新興国市場の有望な投資先だった同国からの資本逃避リスクへの懸念も高まった。投資家によると、新型コロナウイルスのパンデミック以降、プラボウォ大統領の下で財政の健全性や中央銀行の独立性への信頼が薄れる中、同国の魅力は既に低下していた。

事情に詳しい政府当局者２人によると、プラボウォ氏は１９日、財政・金融当局者と会合を開き、「現在の経済情勢」について協議した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・レーティングのソブリン担当アナリスト、レイン・リン氏は、ＭＳＣＩの最新の警告で追加の資本流出が起きる可能性が高いものの、資金調達コストを大幅に押し上げる規模にはならないとの見方を示した。「より懸念されるのは、投資家の信頼が損なわれる可能性と、国債市場や海外直接投資にも投資家心理の悪化が広く波及するリスクだ」と述べた。

ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩ指数から完全に除外されれば、パッシブ運用資金が５６億ドル流出する可能性があると推計。これらの指数をベンチマークとするアクティブ運用ファンドの保有額は８０億ドルを超えるものの、売却するかどうかは指数への連動ではなく、運用者の裁量によると記した。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株を４９億８０００万ドル売り越している。年間の資金流出額は少なくとも過去１６年で最大となるペースだ。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：北朝鮮が韓国と対立姿勢、米国にとって新たな悩みの種に 焦点：新興国投資ラッシュに取り残されるインドネシア、強い政策への不信感 アングル：スマトラ島豪雨被害、森林破壊で被害拡大か　地元に怒りの声 アングル：石炭依存の東南アジア、長期電力購入契約がエネ移行の妨げに 最終更新: 10/19(月) 22:13 ロイター

item.dc:creator: Sonja Wind

item.title: Germany's Merck buys Silence Therapeutics in $1.3 billion RNA drug deal
item.description: German drugmaker Merck KGaA said on Monday it would acquire UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal for about $1.3 billion, bolstering its pipeline of precision medicines and adding RNA-targeting drug technology.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: German drugmaker Merck KGaA (MRCG.DE) said on Monday it would acquire UK-based Silence Therapeutics in an all-cash deal for about $1.3 billion, bolstering its pipeline of precision medicines and adding RNA-targeting drug technology. Merck will pay $20 per American depositary share for Silence, representing a premium of 130% to the stock's last close. US-listed shares of Silence more than doubled in morning trading. The deal broadens Merck's gene-silencing capabilities by adding Silence's siRNA medicines, which work by switching off disease-related gene messages before they can produce harmful proteins. RNA, or ribonucleic acid, is a molecule that carries genetic instructions and helps tell cells which proteins to make. This is Merck's third major acquisition in less than two years, following its $3.9 billion purchase of SpringWorks Therapeutics in 2025 and its pending $11.3 billion takeover of life-sciences tools maker [USN:L8N42X0VJ TEXT:"Bio-Techne"]. Silence's lead therapy candidate, divesiran, is expected to enter late-stage testing for phlebotomy-dependent polycythemia vera, or PV, a rare blood cancer in which the bone marrow produces too many red blood cells. Patients with this condition require regular therapeutic blood draws, known as phlebotomies, to manage their red blood cell levels. With an approval, the drug would compete with Takeda (4502.T) and Protagonist's (PTGX.O) rival drug, Mimrylo. "With Takeda implying $1 billion to $2 billion in peak sales for Mimrylo in PV, the deal valuation does appear inexpensive considering Merck KGaA also gets the broader mRNAi GOLD siRNA platform as well," said William Blair analyst Myles Minter. Minter said the deal "takes the execution risk off the table in an increasingly competitive space". Silence is also developing zerlasiran for people with high lipoprotein(a), a blood protein linked to heart disease, along with earlier-stage treatments for high cholesterol, obesity and immune-related diseases. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The companies said the transaction will be effected through a UK scheme of arrangement.

item.title: Trump geothermal lease sale collides with planned Nevada solar farms
item.description: The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects fromNextEra Energy and other developers, according to federal documents.
item.dc:creator: Nichola Groom
item.content:encoded: The US Interior Department's sale of geothermal leases in Nevada this week will include thousands of acres overlapping major planned solar projects from NextEra Energy (NEE.N) and other developers, according to federal documents. On Tuesday, the Interior Department's Bureau of Land Management is scheduled to auction 83 parcels totaling 265,691 acres to geothermal developers. NextEra, the world's largest owner of solar and wind generation, asked the agency earlier this year to "remove, defer or reconfigure" three proposed geothermal parcels. President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:S0N3RO0B5 TEXT:"promoted"] geothermal energy as a source of always-on electricity while largely [USN:L1N3X1119 TEXT:"excluding"] wind and solar from a broad effort to accelerate federal permitting. In comments submitted to the agency during review of the sale, NextEra said the parcels in question overlap roughly 6,000 acres, or about 60%, of its planned 1,000-megawatt Sawtooth Energy Center in Nye County, Nevada. BLM declined NextEra's request in August, saying federal lands are managed for multiple uses. Maps published on the BLM website in August show overlaps involving six proposed geothermal parcels and four major planned solar developments in the Nevada desert. One parcel, which overlaps entirely with NextEra's Sawtooth project, did not appear on the auction website and appeared to have been recently removed from the sale. NextEra, based in Juno Beach, Florida, said in its comments that the overlap could "create a foreseeable conflict" with its pending application. "NextEra must collaborate with any potential lessee and adjust its operations accordingly to avoid land use conflicts," the agency said. BLM added that if NextEra's project is approved first, it would have the "senior right" and a geothermal development would have to avoid impacts on its project. Another solar developer, Dallas-based Leeward Renewable Energy, said a geothermal parcel overlaps about 735 acres of its proposed Lone Mountain solar project in Esmeralda County. It urged the agency to recognize the overlap "and the non-exclusive nature of any future geothermal lessee's development rights." The agency added a description and maps of the overlapping projects to its sale documents. They include the proposed 300-MW Nivloc solar project being developed by Invenergy and Arevia Power's 1,500-MW Gold Dust solar project. Along with Lone Mountain, those projects were part of the Esmeralda 7 development, a proposed complex of seven solar farms on 62,000 acres. BLM canceled the environmental review for the complex in 2025 but said the projects may reapply for federal approval individually. NextEra, Leeward and BLM did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: 中国人民銀、翌日物リバースレポ金利を主要政策金利に検討中
item.description: [北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、主要政策金利を翌日物リバースレポ金利に切り替えることを...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国人民銀、翌日物リバースレポ金利を主要政策金利に検討中 10/19 19:40 配信

北京の中国人民銀行本部、2025年5月撮影 REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

[北京／上海 １９日 ロイター] - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が、主要政策金利を翌日物リバースレポ金利に切り替えることを検討している。国営メディアが１９日に報じた。金融政策の伝達メカニズムを改善し、経済を下支えすることを目的とした方針転換となる。

中国では２０２４年以来、７日物リバースレポ金利が主要政策金利として機能してきた。

人民銀が運営する「金融新聞」によると、人民銀の潘功勝総裁は、この主要政策金利の変更は人民銀による短期金利のコントロール精度を高める取り組みの一環だとした。

同紙によると、北京で開催された主要な金融フォーラムで、潘氏は「現在、銀行間翌日物レポ金利は事実上、人民銀の金融政策における目標金利となっている」と発言。「この金利は短期流動性の需給を敏感に反映しており、近年はより高い安定性を示している」と語り、翌日物金利を主要金利とすることで金利管理がより精密になるとした。

この政策転換により、人民銀は流動性状況をより的確にコントロールできるようになり、その政策枠組みは世界の他の中央銀行とより整合性を持つようになる。

米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）などの中央銀行は、イールドカーブをより確実に定着させるため、すでに翌日物金利を主要な政策金利として採用している。

発表後、中国の３０年物国債利回りは１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）以上低下した。

国泰君安国際のチーフエコノミスト、周浩氏は「金融政策の枠組みが海外と整合することになり、人民元の国際化を推進する上でよりスムーズになるだろう」と述べた。

金融情報サービス大手の中誠信国際のチーフマクロアナリスト、王青氏は、翌日物リバースレポの実際の運用金利は人民銀が切り替えを行う際に発表されるとし、今回の変更は利下げに相当するものではないと指摘した。

中国のインターバンク市場は潤沢な資金供給が続いている。翌日物レポ金利の平均は約１．２５％と約５カ月ぶりの低水準付近にあり、人民銀の翌日物リバースレポ操作における借入コストとして報じられている水準にほぼ沿っている。これは、現在１．４％となっている７日物リバースレポ金利を下回っている。

今回の変更は中国の金融構造の変化とも整合する。中国では、債券や株式を通じた直接金融が従来型の銀行融資を上回り、新規資金調達の主要な供給源となりつつあり、与信配分も不動産など与信依存度の高いセクターから徐々に離れつつある。

翌日物リバースレポ操作は、人民銀の政策手段に加わった最新のツールとして６月下旬に導入された。

翌日物取引は中国のインターバンク短期金融市場におけるレポ取引高の８割超を占めている。

潘氏は、人民銀は貸出金利ベンチマークの改革を推進するため、今後政策指針を示すと述べた。この改革では、融資における最優遇貸出金利（ＬＰＲ）への比較的高い依存度合いを引き下げ、より多様化したベンチマークへの移行を進める。

同氏は、財務体質が良好な一部の企業は金融機関との協議を経て、変動金利融資の基準として銀行間翌日物レポ金利かＬＰＲのいずれかを選択できるようになる可能性があると述べた。

同氏はまた、人民銀は常設貸出ファシリティー（ＳＬＦ）の利用資格を有する金融機関の範囲を拡大し、非銀行系金融機関向けの流動性支援ツールを設ける予定だと述べた。これらの措置は、保険会社やファンド運用会社を含むノンバンク系金融機関への流動性支援を強化することを目的としている。

item.title: 経産省、ラピダスに27年度から3年で4000億円の産業投資計画
item.description:
Kentaro Okasaka
[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 経済産業省は１９日、先端半導体の量産を目指すラピダス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
経産省、ラピダスに27年度から3年で4000億円の産業投資計画 10/19 19:27 配信

2026年8月21日、都内の本社で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 １９日 ロイター] - 経済産業省は１９日、先端半導体の量産を目指すラピダス（東京都千代田区）向けに、２０２７ー２９年度に産業投資として計４０００億円の出資を要求する計画を明らかにした。財政制度等審議会（財務相の諮問機関）の財政投融資分科会への説明資料で明らかになった。

政府はこれまでに計２５００億円をラピダスに出資しており、今回の産業投資計画が全て実施された場合、累計出資額は６５００億円となる。経産省は、ラピダスが民間融資を受けるためには一定の自己資本比率の維持が必要と指摘。「事業が進捗し、リターンの見通しが相対的に高まっている」とラピダスへの投資意義を説明した。

資料によると、昨年、民間金融機関からラピダスへ２兆円の融資に関する法的拘束力のない意向表明書が発出され、融資実行についての調整・交渉を実施中という。

item.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada, CBC News says
item.description: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation, CBC News said late Monday, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid an ongoing trade war with the US.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Stephenson, Maria Cheng
item.content:encoded: Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on [USN:L6N3Z2101 TEXT:"separation"], CBC News said late Monday, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid an ongoing [USN:SPN44J009 TEXT:"trade war "]with the US. The [USN:L6N46019J TEXT:"referendum"] was nonbinding and asked residents if they wanted to stay part of Canada or start the legal process required to have a binding vote on separation. Pollsters and analysts had repeatedly dismissed the possibility of a separatist victory, citing data that showed about one-third of residents in the Western province supported having a future referendum over leaving the province.
